correctness.rationale: The Fu--Liu--Li centered-triple condition is exactly transformed by x=u, y=-v into N(x)=N(y)=N(x-y)=1 with objective N(x+y). Every admissible pair therefore lies in one of the 1000 faces obtained by choosing one tight signed facet in each sphere constraint. The exact Q(sqrt(5)) checker proves that 60 faces are nonempty and all are segments. On a segment the objective is the maximum of ten affine functions; hence its maximum is at an endpoint, and its minimum is at an endpoint or a pairwise affine-function crossing. Exhausting these candidates gives exactly (9-sqrt(5))/4 and 4-sqrt(5). The explicit attaining pairs are independently checked.
risks: The proof is computation-assisted, but the computation is exact and exhaustive over the continuum reduction rather than a finite sample.
The affine presentation is not the Euclidean-coordinate regular decagon, but it is linearly equivalent to one; the constants are invariant under linear isometry.

originality.rationale: The defining 2021 open full text was inspected through the definitions, examples and conclusion, and targeted searches for decagon, regular polygon, J_L, Y_J, g_1 and J_1 found no covering value. The 2024 Martini--Papini--Wu paper is highly relevant because it studies the same constants under g_1,J_1 notation; only its bibliographic record, abstract and citation snippets were publicly retrievable, and none states a decagonal computation. Its inaccessible full text is explicitly retained as a residual risk rather than treated as a negative whole-document check. published-finding corpus searches under exact invariant and polygon aliases returned no same-invariant decagonal finding.

The full text of the 2024 Martini--Papini--Wu paper was not publicly retrievable; an equivalent decagonal calculation under g_1,J_1 notation could therefore have escaped inspection.

value.rationale: The constants quantify the complete side-length range of centered unit triangles, and the regular decagon is a canonical non-Hilbert, non-parallelogram polyhedral plane. The result gives both endpoints exactly rather than a one-off witness. It also supplies a natural benchmark complementary to the already-studied James and Banach--Mazur geometry of the same decagonal space. The finite-facet method is reusable for centered-triangle constants on other polygonal norms.
risks: The finding is a canonical exact benchmark rather than a classification across all regular polygons.
